calibration_panel.statement: maintainer: the anchor (0 on every board), the sentinel models whose shared listing defines the core boards, and the panel members, declared (owner 2026-11-18: the members of v0.7.0, the panel the owner's hand-written levels were set against). A row listed on every core board does not join the panel; only the owner changes `members`; a member a core board does not list is an error (calibration/measurements.py). Members changed by the owner on 2026-11-19: muse-spark-1.3 replaces deepseek-v4.1-flash-free, because no single snapshot of DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is listed on every core board

effort_readings.statement: maintainer: how a board's listing labels read, one rule for every model. `labels`: a reasoning label and the effort it reads; "(Non-reasoning)", "(Non-Thinking)" and "(Instant)" are reasoning switched off (owner, 2026-11-19, round 6 item 5: the boards' names for a model's thinking-off mode), the `none` effort, whatever effort the tag names besides (of several such listings the bare one, then the one at the effort `default` reads); "(Reasoning)" without an effort is a listing without an effort label, and a listing that names the effort wins over it. `reads`: an effort name off the scale and the measured effort it reads; a listing without an effort label is the model's one configuration, stored under `default` and read at that effort (calibration/measurements.py, calibration/five_axis.py aa_rows and time_rows; five-axis-scores.json `effort_readings`, axis_scores.reading_effort). Where `none` sits, from the vendors' documents: OpenAI's reasoning guide gives `none` for "tasks that do not benefit from any reasoning"; MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, whose "Thinking cannot be turned off", answers `effort: "none"` with `400`, so `none` is the off switch a model may lack; Magpie offers `none` as the off level of a model with a thinking switch; Google's thinking guide calls `minimal` "a near-off setting", a reasoning level above off.

families.statement: maintainer: ordered model-family patterns for names the catalog has no row or alias for; the first pattern matching the bare name decides, and the name resolves to the first listed model the catalog has (an empty list: unknown) (scripts/model_resolution.py). Every row declares the `maker`, the product `line` and the `size` class of the names it decides (owner, 2026-11-19): a row's relatives for an ability facet are the same maker's rows of the same size, every line; for responsiveness, Time/Task and cost per hour only those of its own line (calibration/series.py). A line name shared by two rows is one line across versions (gpt-5.6 and gpt-6 `sol`, `terra`, `luna`; gpt-5.x and gpt-6 `pro`). `small` names are never relatives of `full` ones. `tier_up` on a small row names the pattern of the same line's next larger row, whose first catalogued model is, for a listed member of the small row, its larger model of the same version (calibration/series.py tier_up, five_axis.py tier_down); tier_up_version says whether the larger row's first model is the same version as the small row's current members (`same`) or the nearest version of the same line (`nearest`), calibration/series.py. `tier_up_older` on such a row names, for an older member of the row's line that is not a current member, its larger model and whether it is the same version (`same`) or the nearest (`nearest`). Gemini 4 Neon (owner, 2026-11-19) has a row of its own, `size: full`, resting on two vendor sentences, not on its name: Google's model card (https://deepmind.google/models/model-cards/gemini-4-neon/, published 18 November 2026) "Gemini 4 Neon is adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon", and Google's choosing-a-model page (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/choosing-a-model) "Sits between Hydrogen and Carbon, with deeper reasoning than Hydrogen"; no Google page states its size. `^gemma` is `small` like the other open-weights rows of 26 to 35 billion parameters (`^qwen[\d.]+-\d+b`), and `^gpt-oss-20b` no longer matches gpt-oss-120b, which `^gpt-oss.*20b` did (owner, 2026-11-19: sizes declared uniformly).

series_versions.statement: maintainer: the version number each series row's vendor model id carries, read as a decimal number (Grok 4.20 is 4.2, before 4.3; a dated release, Ministral 2512, is its date); a row without an entry declares none (a moving name, a dated id beside numbered ones, a size rather than a version). The version distance of two rows of one series is how many distinct declared versions of that series lie between them plus one (0: the same version); calibration/series.py nearest orders a row's relatives by it (round 5 review D)

estimation_order.statement: maintainer (round 5 review D): the order of the estimation methods follows their measured error; the refresh never reorders them by itself: a release re-measures with audit/estimation_loo.py and the order changes only by editing this declaration and calibration/five_axis.py together
order: sibling_shift up to the declared version distance
estimation_order.evidence: leave-one-out over the measured High cells of the shipped build (audit/estimation_loo.py, 2026-11-19, relatives by declared maker, line and size, round 6 item 4), median absolute error in panel z: panel effort step 0.221 (n=345), sibling at version distance 0 0.338 (n=156), fleet edge step 0.270 (n=143), sibling d=1 0.408 (n=149), tier fit 0.470 (n=292), sibling d>=2 0.715 (n=14), own ability median 0.637 (n=326), tier down 0.655 (n=13), size step same version 0.871 (n=20), size step nearest version 0.716 with p90 7.66 (n=21); on the same cells the sibling beats the tier fit at distance 0 (0.328 against 0.498, n=128) and 1 (0.297 against 0.455, n=103) and the tier fit wins from distance 2 (0.631 against 0.667, n=11); responsiveness from the own line 0.785 against another line of the same maker and size 1.029 on the same 29 cells. The same-version relations (tier down, size step same version) stay where the owner put them (round 5 review D)

creative_ideation.scope: Cross-domain association, de-novo concept or mechanism invention, creative writing, narrative dialogue, and open-ended brainstorming.

architecture_reasoning.scope: First-principles system architecture, formal or mathematical reasoning, trade-off critique, and multi-system design planning without modifying source code.

code_implementation.scope: Write, fix, refactor, or test backend, CLI, library, algorithm, configuration, or quantitative/experiment code.

frontend_ui.scope: Implement, refactor, or style user-facing web or desktop UI views, interactive components, charts, layouts, CSS, and animations.

code_audit.scope: Independent read-only review or audit of code, pull requests, diffs, branches, security invariants, or release readiness (including writing a review report file).

exploration_forensics.scope: Read-only codebase exploration, log/database/metric forensics, and runtime root-cause diagnosis on local evidence without modifying code.

web_research.scope: Gather, verify, and synthesize information from the public web, literature, documentation, or vendor sources into a sourced report.

visual_analysis.scope: Static offline inspection of images, photos, screenshots, or design mockups: OCR, UI layout/mockup diffs, and fine-grained aesthetic, styling, material, or lighting classification.

text_processing.scope: Rule-defined structured text cleaning, translation, format conversion, mechanical extraction, and bounded summarization.

live_loop.scope: Low-latency observe-decide-act loop attached to a live external text, WebSocket, or API stream where per-turn response time affects the outcome.

gui_control.scope: Operate a live desktop, browser, or mobile graphical interface via screenshots, mouse clicks, and keyboard actions, or continuously monitor a live visual screen.

other_or_mixed.scope: Unprofiled fallback route when no canonical work_kind was supplied.
